identity.name: Jimmy Cobb
home_scenes: The Miles Davis sextet and quintet (1958-1963)
identity.summary: The drummer on Kind of Blue. Cannonball Adderley brought him to Miles Davis in 1958, replacing Philly Joe Jones, and he stayed until Tony Williams came in in 1963: Kind of Blue, Sketches of Spain, Someday My Prince Will Come, the Blackhawk and Carnegie Hall. Then he went on with Wynton Kelly and Paul Chambers as a trio, behind Wes Montgomery among others, and later Sarah Vaughan and the Great Jazz Trio. A light, singing ride with the hi-hat foot on 2 and 4, the bass drum feathered, few comps and those on the swung "and"s, brushes on the themes: 'subtle and understated' (Wikipedia). NEA Jazz Master, 2009; the last of the Kind of Blue players, he died in 2020.

traditions.tradition: Swing and bebop on the radio
traditions.impact: Jazz records and Symphony Sid's late-night broadcasts from New York, heard as a boy in Washington.

formative_events.event: Began touring with Earl Bostic; then Dinah Washington.
Joined Miles Davis in May on Cannonball Adderley's recommendation, replacing Philly Joe Jones.
Left Davis when Tony Williams came in; formed a trio with Wynton Kelly and Paul Chambers.

eras.label: Miles Davis
eras.context: The sextet with Adderley, Coltrane and Evans, then the quintet with Kelly and Chambers.

eras.label: The Wynton Kelly trio
eras.context: Kelly's own records from Kelly Blue, then the trio as a unit after Davis, behind Wes Montgomery, Kenny Burrell and Joe Henderson.
defining_traits: the ride and the comps on the "and"s

swing.notes: Triplet swing at medium tempos (Galaher writes the ride and the comps in triplets); even eighths in All Blues. Estimates.

dynamics.balance: The ride on top, the snare and bass drum under it; the bass drum feathered and dropped in for accents.

feel_profile.interaction: An accompanist first: the snare answers the horns in short comps, mostly on the swung "and"s of 2 and 4 (Galaher's 'Left Hand-Right foot dialogue'), and whole choruses go by on the ride alone.

hand_techniques.name: Comping in triplets
hand_techniques.description: The snare on the last triplet of a beat, alone or with the first; the bass drum joining on the beat between.

hand_techniques.name: Brushes
hand_techniques.description: Brushes behind the themes of So What and All Blues, and through Blue in Green.

hand_techniques.name: Press rolls
hand_techniques.description: A press roll into the next chorus (Ah-Leu-Cha, bars 48 and 63-64).

hand_techniques.name: Cross-stick on 4
hand_techniques.description: A cross-stick on 4 of every bar for whole choruses behind Kelly (Kelly Blue).

foot_techniques.name: The hi-hat foot on 2 and 4
foot_techniques.description: In every transcription and tab, under the ride.

coordination.notes: The ride and the foot as an ostinato under the left hand and the bass drum.

searched: Songsterr: So What (400187), All Blues (462015), Blue in Green (73923), Kelly Blue (902578), Unit 7 (6143491), Four on Six (6155515)
devices_search.note: No device found: no groupings, cross-rhythms or displacements in the time or the comps transcribed.

voice_language.ride: The swing ride with its skip on the "and"s of 2 and 4, light and even; quarters in Kelly Blue's head.
voice_language.snare: Short comps on the swung "and"s; a cross-stick on 4 for a chorus; press rolls into a chorus.
voice_language.kick: Feathered; dropped in on 2, 3 or 4 with the snare.
voice_language.cymbals: A crash on 1 of a soloist's first chorus (So What).

implements.notes: Brushes on the themes and the ballads, sticks for the solos.

sound_profile.cymbal_character: A dark ride, by a forum's account an 18in old K. Zildjian, with a 20in A. Zildjian for accents.

sample_hints.jazz: A small jazz kit, an open bass drum played softly, a dark old ride, brushes for the ballads.

signature_traits.label: The ride and the foot, and little else
signature_traits.description: Choruses on the ride and the hi-hat foot alone, the snare saying something only now and then, on the swung "and"s.

signature_traits.label: The crash into Miles's solo
signature_traits.description: So What: the brushed theme gives way to a crash on 1 of Davis's solo, and the sticks.

signature_traits.label: Brushes for the theme, sticks for the solos
signature_traits.description: All Blues and So What open on brushes and change to sticks for Davis's solo.

patterns.name: Ah-Leu-Cha: the ride, the foot and the answers
patterns.function: The ride's skip in triplets, the foot on 2 and 4, the snare on the "and" of 2 and on 4 (bars 2 and 19-23 of the transcription); then the triplet in both hands with the middle left out, the bass drum on 2 and 4 (bars 29-32).

patterns.name: So What: the band's two notes
patterns.function: The ride rhythm, the foot on 2 and 4, the snare and bass drum together on 3 and the "and" of 4 with the band's answer, then a bar of time: the tab's figure for the theme and the solos.

evidence.note: A human tab; it writes the ride rhythm on an open hi-hat, where the record has a cymbal brushed in the theme (Vintage Drum Forum).

patterns.name: All Blues: the cymbal on 2 and 3
patterns.function: The cymbal on 2 and 3, the snare and the hi-hat foot on 3, in 3/4 with even eighths (the tab), the 6/8 blues of the liner notes; now and then the cymbal on 1, the "and" of 2 and the "and" of 3, the foot on 2.

evidence.note: A loose human tab, the shapes it returns to.

patterns.name: Kelly Blue: the cross-stick on 4
patterns.function: The ride's skip and the foot on 2 and 4, a cross-stick on 4 of every bar, through Kelly's fifth and sixth choruses.

affiliations.name: Wynton Kelly trio
affiliations.notes: With Wes Montgomery, Kenny Burrell, Joe Henderson and others.

evidence.note: In the Miles Davis sextet, May 1958.

philosophy.idea: Taught at Stanford, UNC Greensboro and Berklee.

innovations: The time on the best-selling jazz record: a model of understated swing
common_misconceptions: That his playing on Kind of Blue is all of him: at Newport in 1958 he 'could burn too' (Not So Modern Drummer).

beatbreaker.default_kit_sound: A small jazz kit with a dark ride and a softly played bass drum; brushes for the ballad
generation_rules: The ride with its skip and the hi-hat foot on 2 and 4 under everything.
Few comps, on the swung "and"s, the bass drum dropping in on a beat now and then.
No crashes off the beat; a crash on a chorus's 1 now and then.
Each song in its own grid: All Blues in 3/4 with even eighths, Blue in Green in 12/8 on brushes.
avoid: A bass drum heard on every beat

lineage_display.lineage_blurb: Philly Joe Jones's successor in Miles Davis's band and Tony Williams's predecessor: the quiet middle of the line.
